eli5.text: When the system looked up a saved assistant from its database, the assistant was being rejected by a safety check that expected certain information to be present, so it would fail even though it was valid. eli5.text: This update improves the Freebuff coding assistant for developers, with better support for JavaScript projects, smoother agent behavior, and performance upgrades. The SDK now works with both modern and legacy code setups (ESM and CJS), and includes its own bundled search tool so you don't need to install anything extra. A new agent lookup tool lets you quickly get details about available AI agents, and base agents can now spawn any other agent automatically. The web-based agent store loads faster with static rendering and shows twice as many agents per page, and various backend fixes make streaming responses and error handling more reliable. Upgrading gives you a faster, more flexible experience whether you are coding locally, integrating the SDK into your app, or browsing agents in the store.

ai.title: Add Suspense boundaries to profile and new publisher pages
ai.summary: Wrapped `ProfilePage` and `CreatePublisherPage` in `Suspense` boundaries. This prevents hydration and build errors caused by `useSearchParams` usage in client components without a fallback. The change applies to `web/src/app/profile/page.tsx` and `web/src/app/publishers/new/page.tsx`. Skeleton loaders serve as fallbacks during the suspense state.

eli5.text: When you open your profile or start creating a new publisher, the page will now show a simple loading placeholder (like a gray box) instead of breaking while it gathers info from the address bar. This wraps those two pages in a built-in React feature that waits patiently for the address-bar data to load before showing the real content. If you looked, you'd see the gray placeholder appear briefly, then be replaced by the full page. The change went live on 2025-09-24 and affects anyone opening those two pages.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes process that prepares and publishes new versions of the software has been simplified. The release process is already using the new method, so maintainers will see fewer steps and less custom logic when triggering releases.

ai.title: Multi-column layout for custom agents in load-agents.ts
ai.summary: The `displayLoadedAgents` function in `npm-app/src/agents/load-agents.ts` now formats loaded custom agents into a multi-column grid instead of a single comma-separated line. The layout dynamically calculates `terminalWidth` from `process.stdout.columns` (defaulting to 80) and derives `columnWidth` from the longest agent name plus padding. This change saves vertical space when many custom agents are loaded.

eli5.text: When you start a project and the system loads your custom agents, instead of listing all their names in one long comma-separated line, it now arranges them into a neat grid of columns that fits your terminal window. The system measures your screen width and picks column sizes wide enough for the longest agent name, so the listing takes up less vertical space while keeping every name readable.
